articles.title: 'This would definitely help': How Bellingham's underwear billboard ad in New York reflects football's growing US appeal
articles.summary: Jude Bellingham has added another milestone to his growing list of achievements, this time away from the football pitch.
articles.body: Jude Bellingham has added another milestone to his growing list of achievements, this time away from the football pitch. The England and Real Madrid midfielder features on a giant Calvin Klein underwear billboard in Manhattan, New York, joining a list of celebrities who have appeared on the fashion brand's famous SoHo billboard.Measuring 75 feet by 55 feet (22.9 by 16.8 metres), the billboard overlooks one of New York's busiest shopping areas and has drawn crowds of people stopping to take photographs. Bellingham is seen striking his trademark arms-stretched celebration pose, wearing only a pair of white Calvin Klein hip briefs.The billboard has been a landmark in New York's SoHo neighbourhood for 24 years. Spanning roughly five storeys in height and a quarter of a city block in width, it has featured models, actors, singers, athletes and other celebrities over the years. Bellingham's appearance puts him in the company of names such as Bad Bunny, Jeremy Allen White and Justin Bieber.His selection also reflects the growing reach of football in the United States, which co-hosted the World Cup with Mexico and Canada. Bellingham became a social media sensation during the summer tournament, attracting attention for his performances on the pitch and his appearance."We were just in the area, and then my little sister, she was like, 'I got to see the Jude Bellingham poster' -- especially after they beat Mexico in the World Cup, right?" store manager George Lozano, was quoted as saying by news agency AFP."I personally wouldn't think (most Americans) would recognize him. I think it's still growing. It's growing in terms of the US... support for football. But I think now this would definitely help, right?"Not everyone who stopped to see the billboard was familiar with Bellingham. French tourist Roxane Marin, 33, said she liked the England midfielder but that he was not her favourite player."I like him but he's not my favorite," said Marin, who helped steer England to a famous 6-4 victory over France in the third-place playoff with an inspired 98th-minute solo spectacular."I watch football, but I can't remember if I saw that match," she said, as quoted by AFP.Marin said she had come across the billboard by chance, "but I think there are people who come on purpose."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Nations League: How do Northern Ireland replace 'perfect player' Jamie Donley for Hungary visit?
articles.summary: With Jamie Donley suspended for Northern Ireland's Nations League visit to Hungary on Tuesday night, manager Michael O'Neill has a decision to make around a starting striker.
articles.body:
With six of his starting outfield players against Ukraine on Saturday night having gone into the game a yellow card away from suspension, it was always likely that Northern Ireland manager Michael O'Neill would need to reshuffle his team for the Nations League Group B2 finale in Hungary.

That the player who picked up the booking ended up being Jamie Donley, however, has presented the boss with something of a selection conundrum.

The Tottenham Hotspur forward, currently on loan at Luton Town, has started the side's past 10 games at centre-forward, a different role to the deeper position he has more usually occupied in his club career.

With O'Neill having circled through traditional number nine options such as Dion Charles, Jamie Reid and Lee Bonis since returning to the job four years ago, it feels as if Donley has made the shirt his own since being handed the start against Luxembourg 12 months ago.

While the manager has pushed back on the idea that Donley is playing out of position at international level, the one-game ban is certainly an untimely one with the former Leyton Orient and Oxford United loanee's hold-up play in particular against Ukraine showing how much he has grown into the role.

After the 21-year-old had a goal chalked off by the video assistant referee (VAR) on Saturday, he has still scored just once from open play for his country, but there is a growing appreciation that he is asked to bring much more than just goals to the team.

"He's been such a good player for us. Even without the goals, the way he holds the ball up and spreads the play, his movement is just so good. Playing balls in the air, he pins the defender so well," said Fulham midfielder Shea Charles.

"He's got better every game and he's like the perfect player for us."

Watch on BBC iPlayer and BBC One NI from19:15 GMT; Listen on BBC Sounds and BBC Radio Ulster; Watch, listen, live text and clips on BBC Sport app & website

There is no obvious like-for-like replacement in O'Neill's squad for a game in which they need a draw to secure promotion to Nations League A for the first time.

Arsenal's Ceadach O'Neill pulled out of the double-header through injury last week, with Josh Magennis, Callum Marshall and the uncapped pair of Eoin Kenny and Braiden Graham the other strikers in the travelling party.

Similar to the original ask of Donley, there is also an option to move a wide or deeper player such as Isaac Price or Paddy Kelly into a central striking role.

With only three days between games, however, there has been little time to work on such a plan to replace a player whose four Spurs appearances all came under Ange Postecoglou in the 2023-24 season.

"There are other things we can do. We can change the shape a little bit, play with two front players," said O'Neill, who himself is suspended for the game after two bookings and will watch from the stands.

"There's a number of things that we will look at. Obviously the time between the games makes that somewhat more difficult in terms of preparation.

"We'll find hopefully the right player that can first of all fit into what we want to do, but obviously secondly give the opposition some problems as well."

'No point' in NI playing for a draw in Hungary

The 'manager's dream' who has put NI one game from history

Devlin nets winner as NI top Nations League group

'Me and Marshy will probably play rock, paper, scissors'

Nobody in O'Neill's squad has more international caps or goals than Stevenage striker Magennis.

But while the 36-year-old has started 11 games in League One this season, it has been more than three years since he last did so at international level.

"My role has obviously changed since I've come into the squad," said the player with 94 international appearances and 12 goals to his name.

"If Michael wants to play with the target man and with experience, obviously, he's going to go for me. If he wants a like-for-like, he's probably going to go with Marshy [Callum Marshall]. So, me and Marshy will probably play rock, paper, scissors.

"Jamie brings so much to the team, but I don't think there's going to be a drastic downfall if one of us has to step in for us. I think the competition for places in the squad for us is absolutely brilliant and if you get that opportunity, you've just got to take it."

articles.title: Jesus Owono: Gerard Pique says goalkeeper did not deserve 12-match ban for tackle which resulted in death of Jesus de Miguel
articles.summary: FC Andorra owner Gerard Pique says goalkeeper Jesus Owono did not deserve the 12-match suspension he received following his challenge which resulted in the death of Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel.
articles.body:
FC Andorra owner Gerard Pique says goalkeeper Jesus Owono did not deserve the 12-match suspension he received following his challenge which resulted in the death of Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel.

Owono, 25, was sent off after colliding with De Miguel late on in the second-tier match between Andorra and Tenerife on 2 November.

De Miguel died the following day, aged 30, and a disciplinary committee from the Spanish football federation confirmed Owono's ban last week.

In a video posted on social media, Pique said players past and present, plus coaches and other goalkeepers, felt the incident was "an accident".

The former Spain and Barcelona defender added: "I truly believe that imposing the maximum sanction on Jesus for this action puts him in a situation he does not deserve, because he is not to blame for all of this having happened."

Tenerife striker De Miguel dies after on-field collision

Goalkeeper involved in fatal collision gets 12-game ban

The 12-match suspension was the maximum punishment Owono, 25, could have received, as the disciplinary committee could only consider the offence on the pitch and not "the tragic outcome of the incident".

Following the decision, Tenerife manager Alvaro Cervera said he accepted the regulations do not specifically account for what happened, but acknowledged the ban "might feel light".

Pique also highlighted a recent on-field incident in Spain, when Albacete winger Jose Corpas accidentally kicked Sabadell midfielder Quadri Liameed in the head during a Spanish second division match.

Nigerian Liameed was knocked unconscious but was later discharged from hospital following medical checks, while Spaniard Corpas was shown a straight red card and handed a three-match ban.

"Fortunately Quadri is fine, the consequences in this case were not fatal, and the committee decided to sanction Corpas with three matches," Pique said.

"With all this, my reflection is: what is being sanctioned, the action or the consequences?"

Owono has withdrawn from Equatorial Guinea's squad for Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers against Zimbabwe this month, and Pique said it was unlikely he would return to action as soon as his suspension is served.

He added: "Jesus is going to need far more than 12 matches before he is available and able to compete.

"No sanction is going to bring [De Miguel] back to us."

articles.title: Nations League: When is the quarter-final draw?
articles.summary: Our Ask Me Anything Team tell you all you need to know about the Nations League quarter-final draw.
articles.body:
The draw for the final eight teams in the 2026-27 Nations League will be on Friday, 20 November at 11:00 GMT.

It will take place at Uefa's headquarters in Nyon, Switzerland and be broadcast on Uefa TV.

England are the only home nation to have made it to the quarter-final stage, however a win or draw for Northern Ireland against Hungary would see them top Group B2 and be promoted to League A in the 2028-29 tournament.

Scotland will remain in League B following their third-place finish in Group B1, and Wales face a League A/B relegation play-off in March after being consigned to last place in Group A4.

The winners of groups A1-A4 are seeded for the draw, playing the runners-up of other groups in League A.

England have sealed their place in the last eight as Group A3 winners and could face:

They cannot face A3 runners-up Spain as teams must be drawn against sides from other groups.

The quarter-finals will be played over two legs during the international break between 25-30 March.

Seeded teams get to play the second leg of their quarter-final at home.

Nations that reach the semi-finals can bid those penultimate matches as well as the final.

The remaining dates for the Nations League are:

Semi-finals, third-place play-off and final: 9-13 June

articles.title: The Mike Ashley relegations pre Newcastle United takeover and lessons to be learnt
articles.summary: I hold my hands up that I was guilty of a bit of an oversight during The Mag Podcast last week. “Those who do not learn from the past are doomed to repeat it...
articles.body:
I hold my hands up that I was guilty of a bit of an oversight during The Mag Podcast last week.

"Those who do not learn from the past are doomed to repeat it" – George Santayana

I half remembered the quote above and threw it to my co-host Hutch on The Mag Pod to try and recite it verbatim, as he likes history and stuff like that.

There were two errors involved to be fair, me for putting him on the spot like that, and Hutch for being as thick as mince.

Jamie puts Hutch on the spot over Newcastle United's relegation history

Anyway, I've since found the appropriate wording and replicated as a starting point here, as a way of conveying what we've been doing on The Mag Pod as we tried to fill the ongoing international break. Basically, there has been some chatter and paranoia that the issues this Newcastle United side are facing this season could well lead to a relegation battle. If it does turn out that way, it won't be any of our first rodeos.

However, it's fair to say that many of those Mike Ashley era struggles ended fairly benignly, with the drop avoided. On occasions this was comfortably, at times it was squeaky, but it didn't really matter as long as you lived to fight another day. Unfortunately, there were exceptions.

So, to try and learn the lessons of history, we have used this round of podcasts to look at the Mike Ashley seasons where it went terribly wrong.

Late last week the first instalment ( Episode 16 ) dropped, as we took a walk through the chaotic 2008-09 season. The follow-up, reliving the relegation of 2015-16 ( Episode 17 ), which is out now.

These serve as both a wander through times gone by and a study in what we can learn.

Ideally, listeners may feel better about current circumstances in comparison with the poor decisions, awful form and careless business that led to highly avoidable seasons away from the Premier League under the previous regime.

Unfortunately there may be times when certain things ring true and we appear in real danger of breaking Mr Santayana's above rule.

There is a third instalment to come as well, but alas we are a bit wet behind the lugs to fully recount the demotion of 1988-89.

Instead, a slight change of tack is incoming where Thursday's edition (Episode 18) will see a review of the 2020-21 season, the final year before the Newcastle United takeover . This is to give a perspective on how far we have come, the impact of the considerable changes since and to hopefully make you all feel better you're no longer looking at Steve Bruce.

Spoiler alert, but the general overall conclusion of these editions is that more time and consideration is needed in the current circumstances, to really have a full and proper idea of how badly it may compare to some of our darker times. However, there are things in there that may very well resonate.

Please enjoy The Mag Podcast and we'd love your feedback on what we have done so far and suggestions for the future in the commenting section below.

Ep 17: Newcastle United's 2015-16 relegation with lessons from the past

articles.title: Is Vinicius Jr really back? Brazil star scores his first-ever national team hat-trick in under 20 mins after admitting he is only 'human'
articles.summary: Vinicius Jr shines for Brazil with his first international hat-trick in a friendly match against Singapore, showcasing his remarkable return to form after a challenging start to the season.
articles.body: Vinicius Jr needed barely 20 minutes to deliver the kind of performance Brazil have been waiting to see from him, scoring three times against Singapore to take his tally to five goals in two internationals. It marks an encouraging turnaround after a difficult start to the season at Real Madrid, where the forward admitted that his preparation had fallen short of his usual standards, although the quality of opposition means his return to form will be better judged when he resumes club duties.Vinicius Jr ends Brazil's year with first international hat-trickVinicius scored his first hat-trick for Brazil in Tuesday's 7-0 friendly victory over Singapore, completing all three goals inside the opening 20 minutes at the National Stadium.He opened the scoring in the ninth minute, controlling the ball inside the penalty area before turning and sending a low finish towards the right post. Six minutes later, Endrick supplied the assist for his second goal as Brazil broke forward on the counter-attack. Vinicius completed the hat-trick in the 20th minute, this time finishing after a pass from Estevao.It was a remarkably productive opening spell for the Real Madrid forward, who was substituted in the 59th minute after giving Brazil a commanding lead. Endrick, who started alongside him and played the full match, added the fourth shortly before half-time with a powerful left-footed effort from the edge of the penalty area. Estevao and Rayan also scored, while Singapore's Suhaimi put through his own net to complete the 7-0 result.The fixture was the first meeting between Brazil and Singapore, and the hosts were unable to offer much resistance. Singapore are ranked 149th in the world, making this a very different test from the matches Vinicius faces at the highest level of international football.That qualification matters, but so does the confidence the forward can take from the performance. His hat-trick followed a brace against Japan on November 14, when Brazil lost 3-2. Five goals across two matches have given him a strong finish to the international year, even if the two performances came in very different circumstances.A difficult start at Real Madrid made the goals more significantThe sudden burst of international scoring comes after Vinicius acknowledged that his performances at the beginning of the 2026-27 season had fallen below his own expectations.Speaking before the Singapore friendly, the 26-year-old offered a candid explanation for his lack of sharpness. “I trained less, I made mistakes, I’m human,” he said, accepting that his preparation had contributed to his early-season struggles.Brazil's unexpected early exit from the World Cup had taken an emotional toll, and Vinicius admitted that he prioritised rest and time with his family during the off-season instead of following his usual intensive conditioning programme. He recognised that the decision had affected his physical preparation and left him short of the sharpness expected at the start of a new campaign.There were other distractions. Transfer speculation involving rival clubs and uncertainty surrounding his contract renewal at the Bernabeu added to the pressure during the summer. The combination of those issues made the opening months more difficult, although Vinicius remained confident that there was enough time in the season to recover his best form.His three goals against Singapore do not settle the question of whether that recovery has begun. They do, however, offer a more encouraging indication than the performances that preceded them, particularly after he followed his brace against Japan with another three goals just three days later.Brazil's goalscoring run is encouraging, but the bigger test awaitsVinicius has never lacked the ability to produce decisive performances for Real Madrid. He has scored four competitive hat-tricks for the Spanish club: against Levante in 2022, Barcelona in the 2024 Spanish Super Cup final, Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League later that year, and Osasuna in LaLiga in 2024. His three goals against Singapore take his senior career hat-trick tally to five.The international milestone is nevertheless significant. Vinicius has often carried the expectation of being one of Brazil's leading attacking players, but his goalscoring record for the national team has not always reflected the influence he has established at club level. Scoring five times in two November fixtures gives him a welcome boost as Brazil close their 2026 campaign.The next question is whether he can carry that confidence back to Madrid. A hat-trick against Singapore is not proof that his earlier problems have disappeared, and the quality of opposition should temper any suggestion that he has already rediscovered his best level. But his admission about his preparation, followed by consecutive multi-goal performances for Brazil, provides a clearer picture of both what went wrong and what may be changing.Vinicius has acknowledged the mistakes behind his slow start. He now has five goals in two appearances to build on, with Brazil having completed their final match of 2026. The more demanding test comes when he returns to Real Madrid, where he will need to show that this renewed scoring touch can translate into consistent performances at club level.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s mother slams Portugal manager Jorge Jesus
articles.summary: Following an average 2026 FIFA World Cup performance and a below-par UEFA Nations League game, Cristiano Ronaldo announced his retirement from international...
articles.body:
Following an average 2026 FIFA World Cup performance and a below-par UEFA Nations League game , Cristiano Ronaldo announced his retirement from international soccer . Ronaldo was benched during Portugal's second UEFA Nations League game, following which there arose a certain miscommunication between him and Portugal's manager, Jorge Jesus.

After several more back-and-forth exchanges and a press conference, Ronaldo parted ways with the team . He was later fined and suspended from the team; Ronaldo announced his retirement and parted ways with the team after 23 years. A true legend, Ronaldo bid adieu to Portugal as their captain.

Later, after Portugal's 1-4 loss to Denmark, Jesus was asked about his thoughts on Ronaldo's absence and if he missed the legend . "Do I miss him? But what is there to miss? If he's no longer available for the national team, what exactly are we missing? (…) He no longer plays, he's no longer here, and he's already made his decision about his situation," he further added. (quotes translated via X's auto translate)

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

However, Ronaldo's retirement and departure from the Portugal team did not sit well with his mother . Recently, at a sporting event on Monday, Nov. 16, 2026, Dolores Aveiro was asked about her son's national team retirement. "Of course he was sad. They deceived him. And I'm sad, too. The defeat [against Denmark] was well-deserved. I was actually glad," she said (quotes via BBC).

Soon after, before Portugal's Nations League game against Wales in Cardiff, Jesus was asked for his thoughts on Aveiro's comments. "Now I have to respond to Cristiano Ronaldo's mother?" he said. "She is a lady I greatly respect – she suffered a lot to raise her children."

"I don't know when it's going to stop. If you guys ask the questions, I have to answer. If you ask about Ronaldo next year, I will answer," Jesus further answered when asked when questions about Ronaldo's retirement would stop.

Ronaldo, 41, spent over two decades with Portugal's national team and retired after a legendary career consisting of 234 games and 146 goals for his country.

articles.title: Miami Dolphins’ Most Valuable Player | Week Ten | Youth
articles.summary: Chris Johnson has 59-yard interception return for touchdown against Colts.
articles.body:
The Miami Dolphins have been going through a bit of a youth-movement this season, in case you haven't heard. They're the youngest team in the National Football League by a wide margin — with an average age of just over 25 years at the start of the season. They've also had the most snaps taken by rookie players out of any NFL team this season — leading the Cleveland Browns by a comfortable amount.

That emphasis on developing young players is paying off for the Dolphins in a major way. While the team is currently struggling in the standings — winning just one game on the year so far — their rookies are taking their lumps and learning the ropes at an expedited pace. That should help the team progress much quicker than most anticipate, while keeping their future cap situation in the good (and cheap) place.

Miami Dolphins Week Nine MVP – Cornerback Chris Johnson

One young player who has been excelling in Jeff Halfey's defensive scheme is rookie first-rounder Chris Johnson. Miami's young cornerback has two interceptions on the season after nabbing one against Daniel Jones of the Colts on Sunday. He returned that interception 59-yards for a touchdown — Miami's first pick-6 on the year. In addition to his two interceptions, Johnson also has a forced fumble during his rookie campaign.

Following the game, Johnson spoke about how coaching helped him make his stellar play on Sunday.

"Definitely felt good. Really just reading my keys. Once the quarterback scrambles, he's looking to get the ball out of his hands. That's kind of something we talked about throughout the week. When we get him off-schedule, it's an opportunity. Really just making the most of my opportunity in that situation."
